questions.q: A managed table in Unity Catalog is dropped. What happens to its data files?

options.t: They are deleted immediately, with no way to recover the table
options.why: Files are deleted after a recovery period, during which UNDROP works.

options.t: They are deleted after a recovery period; UNDROP TABLE works within it
They stay in storage forever, because Unity Catalog never deletes files
options.why: For managed tables, Unity Catalog deletes the files after the recovery period.

options.t: They are moved to the workspace's trash folder for 30 days
options.why: There is no trash folder; a recovery period with UNDROP TABLE applies.

questions.explain: Managed tables get automatic file deletion after DROP TABLE once a recovery period ends (default 7 days); UNDROP TABLE recovers the table within it.

questions.q: An external table in Unity Catalog is dropped. What happens to its data files?

options.t: They are deleted together with the table's metadata
options.why: Dropping an external table removes metadata and leaves the files.

options.t: They are moved into the schema's managed storage location
options.why: Nothing is moved; the files stay where they are.

options.t: They stay where they are; only the metadata is removed
They are deleted after a 7-day recovery period, as with managed tables
options.why: The recovery-period deletion applies to managed tables.

questions.explain: Unity Catalog manages only an external table's metadata; dropping it removes the metadata and leaves the files.

questions.q: Which table type does Databricks call the default and recommended one?

options.t: External tables, because the files stay under your control
options.why: Managed tables are the default and recommended type.

options.t: Hive metastore tables, for compatibility with older workloads
options.why: The legacy Hive metastore is still supported, but Unity Catalog managed tables are recommended.

options.t: Foreign tables reached through Lakehouse Federation
options.why: Federation reads external systems; managed tables are the default.

options.t: Managed tables

questions.explain: Managed tables are the default and recommended table type: Unity Catalog manages reads, writes, storage and optimization, and they cost less to store and query.

questions.q: Which feature is available to Unity Catalog managed tables but not to external tables?

options.t: Predictive optimization
Time travel to earlier versions of the table
options.why: Delta time travel works on external Delta tables too.

options.t: Grants with SELECT and MODIFY on the table
options.why: Both table types are securables you can grant on.

options.t: Storing data as Parquet files under the Delta log
options.why: Both can be Delta tables built on Parquet files.

questions.explain: Features only managed tables get include predictive optimization, automatic liquid clustering, multi-statement transactions, metadata caching and automatic file deletion after DROP.

questions.q: When are external tables the right choice, according to Databricks?

options.t: Whenever the data is larger than a terabyte, for performance
options.why: Size isn't the criterion; managed tables are the default.

options.t: When non-Databricks clients must read the files directly, or the format can't be a managed table
Whenever you need row filters and column masks on the table
options.why: Fine-grained controls work on managed tables too.

options.t: For every bronze table, because Databricks requires raw bronze data never to be deleted by a DROP
options.why: That isn't a documented rule; managed tables are the default.

questions.explain: Use external tables for existing data in a format managed tables can't hold, or for direct access from non-Databricks clients.

questions.q: An external engine reads an external table's files straight from ADLS. Do the table's Unity Catalog grants apply to that access?

options.t: Yes, because Unity Catalog checks every read of the storage account
options.why: Unity Catalog privileges are not enforced on direct file access.

options.t: Yes, but only for SELECT; MODIFY isn't checked on direct reads
options.why: Direct file access bypasses Unity Catalog privileges entirely.

options.t: Only if the external location has row filters attached
options.why: Direct file access isn't governed by Unity Catalog grants.

options.t: No: Unity Catalog privileges aren't enforced on direct file access

questions.explain: Unity Catalog privileges are not enforced on direct file access to an external table's files.

questions.q: Which command converts a Delta external table to a managed table while keeping its history and permissions?

options.t: CREATE TABLE new_t AS SELECT * FROM t, then drop t
options.why: CTAS works but loses history and the other benefits.

options.t: ALTER TABLE t SET MANAGED
ALTER TABLE t SET TBLPROPERTIES ('type' = 'MANAGED')
options.why: The command is ALTER TABLE ... SET MANAGED.

options.t: CONVERT TO DELTA t, which converts it to managed
options.why: CONVERT TO DELTA turns Parquet into Delta; it doesn't make a table managed.

questions.explain: ALTER TABLE t SET MANAGED converts a Delta external table to managed (DBR 17.3 LTS+ or serverless; you must own it), keeping name, settings, permissions, views and history.

questions.q: A table was converted with SET MANAGED last week and must be rolled back to external. What is the documented way?

options.t: RESTORE TABLE t TO VERSION AS OF the version before the conversion
options.why: The documented rollback is ALTER TABLE t UNSET MANAGED.

options.t: DROP the table and recreate it as external from the old path
options.why: UNSET MANAGED rolls back without dropping.

options.t: ALTER TABLE t UNSET MANAGED, within 14 days
It can't be rolled back once converted to managed
options.why: Rollback is possible within 14 days with UNSET MANAGED.

questions.explain: Roll back within 14 days with ALTER TABLE t UNSET MANAGED; writes made after the conversion are kept.

questions.q: What happens to writes made after a SET MANAGED conversion if the table is rolled back with UNSET MANAGED?

options.t: They are lost, and the table returns to its pre-conversion state
options.why: Writes made after the conversion are kept.

options.t: They are kept
They are moved to a separate table named t_managed_backup
options.why: No separate table is created; the writes are kept.

options.t: The rollback is blocked until they are deleted by hand
options.why: Rollback works, and writes after the conversion are kept.

questions.explain: ALTER TABLE ... UNSET MANAGED rolls back within 14 days, keeping writes made after the conversion.

questions.q: What privileges does creating an external table need?

options.t: CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE on the external location, plus USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and CREATE TABLE
Only Storage Blob Data Contributor on the storage account
options.why: Azure roles go to the Access Connector; users need Unity Catalog privileges.

options.t: Only ownership of the metastore, since external tables are account-level
options.why: Specific privileges are needed, not metastore ownership.

options.t: READ FILES on the volume that sits in the same path
options.why: External tables need CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE on the external location.

questions.explain: Creating an external table needs CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE on the external location plus USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and CREATE TABLE.

questions.q: What is an external location in Unity Catalog?

options.t: A cloud region where the workspace's metastore is replicated for disaster recovery
options.why: An external location is a storage path plus a credential.

options.t: A schema whose tables are all external
options.why: It is a securable for a storage path, not a kind of schema.

options.t: A Lakehouse Federation connection to another database
options.why: That is a connection.

options.t: A storage path plus the storage credential that can reach it

questions.explain: An external location is a storage path plus its credential; every external table and external volume must sit inside one.

questions.q: On Azure, what does a Unity Catalog storage credential typically use to reach ADLS Gen2?

options.t: The managed identity of an Access Connector for Azure Databricks
The storage account key, stored in the storage credential's properties
options.why: Databricks recommends against account keys; the managed identity is recommended.

options.t: The personal Entra ID login of whoever creates the table
options.why: Storage credentials use a long-term identity such as the Access Connector's managed identity.

options.t: A SAS token that is renewed by a scheduled job every hour
options.why: The recommended credential is a managed identity, with no rotation.

questions.explain: Create an Access Connector (holding a managed identity), grant it a storage role on the ADLS account, and use it in a storage credential.

questions.q: Which Azure role on the ADLS account does the documentation give as an example for the Access Connector's managed identity?

options.t: Owner, so the identity can manage the account's settings
options.why: A data role such as Storage Blob Data Contributor is the example.

options.t: Reader, which allows reading blobs in every container
options.why: Reader is a management-plane role; the example is Storage Blob Data Contributor.

options.t: Storage Blob Data Contributor
Network Contributor, so the identity can reach private endpoints
options.why: That is a networking role, not a data role.

questions.explain: Grant the identity a storage role on the ADLS account, for example Storage Blob Data Contributor (or Storage Blob Delegator on the account plus Contributor on one container).

questions.q: Why does Databricks prefer a managed identity over a service principal's client secret for storage access?

options.t: Managed identities can read any storage account in the tenant
options.why: They get only the roles you grant them.

options.t: Managed identities need no secret rotation and can reach firewalled storage from a VNet-injected workspace
Client secrets can't be used with ADLS Gen2 at all
options.why: They can, in the legacy pattern; managed identities are preferred.

options.t: Managed identities bypass Unity Catalog grants, so setup is simpler
options.why: Access still goes through Unity Catalog privileges.

questions.explain: Managed identities need no secret rotation and can reach a firewall-protected storage account from a VNet-injected workspace.

questions.q: What are Unity Catalog volumes for?

options.t: Storing tables in a faster format than Delta
options.why: Volumes hold non-tabular files, not tables.

options.t: Caching query results on SQL warehouses
options.why: Volumes govern files in storage, not caches.

options.t: Governing non-tabular files, accessed by path
Holding cloud credentials for external locations
options.why: That is a storage credential.

questions.explain: Volumes govern non-tabular files of any format, at /Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>/...; files in volumes can't be registered as tables.

questions.q: Which three privileges does a user need to read the table sales.gold.orders?

options.t: SELECT on the table only, since it is the object being read
options.why: USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA are also required.

options.t: USE CATALOG on sales, USE SCHEMA on sales.gold, and SELECT on the table
BROWSE on the catalog, then USE SCHEMA on the schema and SELECT on the table itself
options.why: BROWSE shows that objects exist; USE CATALOG is needed to read.

options.t: MODIFY on the table, plus ownership of the schema it sits in
options.why: MODIFY is for writes; reading needs USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and SELECT.

questions.explain: Reading a table needs SELECT on the table, USE SCHEMA on its schema and USE CATALOG on its catalog.

questions.q: A table owner grants SELECT to the analysts group, but analysts still get a permission error. What is the most likely cause?

options.t: SELECT takes 24 hours to propagate to every workspace
options.why: Grants apply directly; the usual cause is missing usage privileges.

options.t: Analysts also need MODIFY to read a table
options.why: MODIFY is for writes.

options.t: Grants to groups don't work; each analyst needs a personal grant
options.why: Granting to groups is the recommended practice.

options.t: They lack USE CATALOG or USE SCHEMA on the parents

questions.explain: USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA grant no data by themselves; they are boundaries the parents' owners control, and a table owner's SELECT grant is useless without them.

questions.q: SELECT is granted on the schema sales.gold. A new table is created in it next month. Can grantees read the new table?

options.t: No, schema grants cover only tables that existed at grant time
options.why: Privileges on a schema apply to current and future objects.

options.t: Yes, schema privileges apply to current and future objects
Only if the new table's owner re-runs the GRANT on the schema
options.why: Inheritance covers future objects automatically.

options.t: Only if the new table is a view rather than a table
options.why: Inheritance covers every table and view.

questions.explain: A privilege granted on a catalog or schema applies to the current and future objects inside it.

questions.q: Which privilege lets a user insert, update and delete rows in a table?

options.t: WRITE, which is the general data-change privilege for tables and views
options.why: The privilege for data changes is MODIFY.

options.t: OWN, which is granted per table for data changes
options.why: Ownership isn't granted as a privilege; MODIFY allows data changes.

options.t: MODIFY, together with SELECT and the usage privileges
REFRESH, which also covers table data changes
options.why: REFRESH applies to materialized views.

questions.explain: MODIFY on a table allows insert, update and delete, and needs SELECT plus the usage privileges.

questions.q: What does the BROWSE privilege allow?

options.t: Reading the first 100 rows of any table in the catalog
options.why: BROWSE gives no data access.

options.t: Seeing that objects exist and requesting access, without reading data
Browsing files in the catalog's managed storage
options.why: BROWSE concerns metadata visibility, not files.

options.t: Listing other users' grants on the catalog and changing them where needed
options.why: Changing grants needs ownership or MANAGE.

questions.explain: BROWSE (granted on a catalog) lets users see that objects exist and request access without reading data; Databricks recommends granting it to All account users.

questions.q: Which principals can be granted privileges in Unity Catalog?

options.t: Users, groups and service principals
Users only; groups are for workspace access
options.why: Groups and service principals can be granted privileges too.

options.t: Groups only; users must be added to a group
options.why: Users and service principals can also be grantees.

options.t: Service principals only, for automation
options.why: Users and groups are grantees too.

questions.explain: Principals are users, groups and service principals (by application ID).

questions.q: Who can grant privileges on a Unity Catalog table?

options.t: The table's owner
A user with MANAGE on the table
Any user with SELECT on the table
options.why: SELECT doesn't allow granting.

options.t: Any workspace admin of any workspace
options.why: Granting needs ownership, parent ownership, MANAGE or metastore admin.

options.t: Any member of the All account users group
options.why: That group has no special granting rights.

questions.explain: Privileges can be granted by the owner, the owner of the containing catalog or schema, a user with MANAGE on the object, or a metastore admin.

questions.q: The exam guide lists GRANT, REVOKE and DENY. Which statement about DENY in Unity Catalog is accurate?

options.t: DENY is a SQL statement that overrides GRANT on any securable
options.why: Unity Catalog SQL has no DENY statement.

options.t: DENY works like REVOKE but also blocks future grants
options.why: There is no DENY statement in Unity Catalog SQL.

options.t: DENY is required before a REVOKE takes effect
options.why: REVOKE works on its own; there is no DENY statement.

options.t: Unity Catalog SQL has no DENY statement; denial exists only as an ABAC DENY policy (Beta)

questions.explain: There is no DENY statement in Unity Catalog SQL; GRANT, REVOKE and DENY statements belong to legacy Hive metastore table access control. The only Unity Catalog denial is an ABAC DENY policy (Beta), limited to MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL.
